clue.text: At last, floor space charge generates profit

indicators.note: each of the next words gives up its final letter

parts.note: last letter of floor
last letter of space
a ward is a young person in someone's charge

explanation.surface: A landlord makes money by renting out floor space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Floor space charge' reads as one rental fee; it splits into two letter sources and a separate noun, with 'charge' meaning a person looked after.
explanation.definitionFit: A reward is a gain or benefit, which is what profit is in its looser sense.

clue.text: Building problem — slope flanking siding unstable

indicators.note: flanking means standing on either side, so the slope's letters go round the rest

parts.note: a ramp is a slope

indicators.note: unstable suggests the letters of siding are not fixed and get rearranged

explanation.surface: A surveyor notes that a sloping bit of ground beside a railway siding is unstable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unstable' rearranges SIDING into ISINGD, which RAMP flanks: R + ISINGD + AMP.
explanation.definitionFit: Rising damp is moisture creeping up a wall from the ground, a common defect in old buildings.

clue.text: Cheer TV doctor overseeing surgical procedure

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first part sits above the second

parts.note: Doctor Who, the BBC time traveller
op = operation

explanation.surface: A television doctor supervises an operation and there is cause for celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor Who is the long-running BBC science-fiction series; in crosswords 'TV doctor' almost always means WHO.
explanation.definitionFit: To whoop is to give a loud cry of joy, which is to cheer.

clue.text: Abusively criticised bloody despicable cuts

indicators.note: one word cuts into the other, splitting it

parts.note: red = the colour of blood
vile = despicable; it goes inside RE…D

explanation.surface: Someone was savagely attacked in print for making despicable cuts, perhaps to public spending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuts' looks like spending cuts, the thing criticised; it is the instruction for VILE to cut into RED.
explanation.definitionFit: To revile someone is to criticise them in abusive language.

clue.text: Vulgar scheme involves English bishop that is retiring

indicators.note: involves means takes in, so the scheme's letters wrap around the rest

parts.note: a plan is a scheme
B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the letters for 'that is' run backwards

parts.note: i.e. is the Latin abbreviation for 'that is'

explanation.surface: Some coarse plot ends up implicating an English bishop who is about to retire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' is i.e., the Latin abbreviation; the scheme 'involves' everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Plebeian means belonging to the common people, hence coarse or lacking refinement.

clue.text: Uncovered definitive sweet or savoury drink

indicators.note: uncovered means with the outer covering stripped, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: a classic is the definitive example of its kind

explanation.surface: A recipe touts the ultimate drink, which can be had sweet or savoury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncovered' strips the outer letters C and C from CLASSIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassi is an Indian yoghurt-based drink served either sweetened or salted with spices.

clue.text: Unsound victory buries Liberal prime minister

indicators.note: the Liberal is put inside, as a body is put in the ground

parts.note: bad = unsound, as in bad reasoning
L = Liberal, placed inside BA…D
a win is a victory

explanation.surface: A dubious election win sees a Liberal prime minister buried politically.
explanation.walkthrough: Stanley Baldwin was a Conservative prime minister three times between the wars; 'Liberal' in the surface points to the wrong party.
explanation.definitionFit: Stanley Baldwin served as British prime minister in the 1920s and 1930s.

clue.text: Break tile under base

indicators.note: base means debased or corrupted, so the letters are corrupted into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: A tile has cracked underneath, at the base of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break' looks like the instruction to scramble; it is the definition, and the unusual indicator is 'base', in the sense of debased.
explanation.definitionFit: An interlude is an interval or pause, a break between parts of something.

clue.text: New sign put up when Santa comes

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: LEO, a sign of the zodiac, turned upward
N = new

explanation.surface: A new sign is put up to announce Father Christmas's arrival.
explanation.walkthrough: LEO is one of the twelve zodiac signs; in a down clue 'put up' makes it read upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Noël is French for Christmas, used in English carols, and Christmas Eve is the night Santa arrives.

clue.text: Made anxious under previous religious office

indicators.note: in a down clue, this part comes below the next

parts.note: prior = previous
as in 'what's eating you?'

explanation.surface: Someone is fretting over a church post they held before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made anxious' gives ATE through the idiom 'what's eating you?', meaning what is worrying you.
explanation.definitionFit: A priorate is the office or term of a prior in a religious house.

clue.text: Awful slurs — I vow this will eventually plague host

indicators.note: the letters are in an awful mess

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: Someone who has been insulted swears the insults will come back to haunt the person who hosted them.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive rather than a synonym: a slow virus lies dormant a long time before attacking its host.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow virus has a long incubation, so it only eventually makes its host ill.

clue.text: Turner and others reflecting about what gets him going

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the reversed letters go round the next piece
reflecting means mirrored, so the letters for 'and others' read backwards

parts.note: et al is the Latin abbreviation for 'and others'

indicators.note: what gets a word going is its opening letter, so only the start of him is used
going completes the phrase meaning the word's start, so just its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of him is H

explanation.surface: The painter Turner and his fellow artists look back on what motivates him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflecting' turns ETAL into LATE, and 'about' puts it round H, 'what gets' him 'going'. The painter J.M.W. Turner is a decoy: a turner is a machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathe is a machine that turns wood or metal against a cutting tool, so it is literally a turner.

clue.text: Protracted campaigns can now polarise careers

indicators.note: to career is to rush about wildly

parts.note: anagram fodder, 14 letters

explanation.surface: Drawn-out political campaigns can now split people's working lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Careers' reads as a noun; it is a verb, to career, and it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Napoleonic Wars ran from 1803 to 1815, a long series of military campaigns.

clue.text: Sinister individual abandoned description of her?

parts.note: left = abandoned
the word HER spelt out as 'H and ER'

explanation.surface: A menacing man walks out on a woman, and here is what she looks like.
explanation.walkthrough: Sinister is Latin for left, and heraldry still uses it for the left side; so a sinister individual is left-handed, not wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister means on the left, so a sinister person is one who favours the left hand.

clue.text: Psalmist prepared seventeenth-century bible lines

indicators.note: one word lines the other, wrapping round it

parts.note: did = prepared, as in 'did the vegetables'
the Authorised Version of 1611, set inside D…ID

explanation.surface: The writer of the psalms drafts verses for the King James Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lines' looks like the verses of scripture; it is the verb, with DID lining the AV.
explanation.definitionFit: King David is traditionally credited with writing the Psalms.

clue.text: City in which you must be protected by vehicle insurance

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

indicators.note: the letters are sheltered inside the insurance word

parts.note: insurance cover
U = you in text-speak, placed inside CO…VER

explanation.surface: A city where drivers are legally required to have motor insurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You' becomes U as in text messages, and it is the one protected, sitting inside the insurance.
explanation.definitionFit: Vancouver is a city in British Columbia, Canada.

clue.text: Risky undertaking, coming by river

indicators.note: one part set beside the next

parts.note: an advent is an arrival, a coming
the Ure, a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A daring enterprise arrives by way of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a Yorkshire river that crosswords use constantly; 'coming' is a noun here, an arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: An adventure is a bold undertaking with an uncertain, risky outcome.

clue.text: Test 1960s car model — very old Mercedes, essentially

parts.note: the Vauxhall Viva, a British family car launched in 1963
V = very
O = old

indicators.note: take the essence, the letters at the heart of the word

parts.note: the two middle letters of merCEdes

explanation.surface: A road test pits a 1960s saloon against a vintage Mercedes.
explanation.walkthrough: The Vauxhall Viva was a British family car of the 1960s; 'essentially' takes the heart of Mercedes.
explanation.definitionFit: A viva voce is an oral examination, a test conducted by spoken questions.

clue.text: Table designer's almost repaired exposed tube

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: mended means repaired

indicators.note: exposed means with its outer layer removed, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: a sleeve is a tube of fabric, or a tubular casing in engineering

explanation.surface: A furniture maker's work has nearly been repaired, leaving a pipe on show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims MENDED to MENDE; 'exposed' strips SLEEVE to LEEV. The table is the periodic one.
explanation.definitionFit: Dmitri Mendeleev drew up the periodic table of the elements, so he is its designer.

clue.text: Plant centre in New Guinea flourishing

indicators.note: flourishing suggests vigorous movement, so the letters are rearranged
the centre in a three-letter word is its middle letter

parts.note: the middle letter of New is E

explanation.surface: A plant grows at the heart of a thriving New Guinea forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre in' takes E from NEW; 'flourishing' mixes E with GUINEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugenia is a genus of flowering shrubs and trees in the myrtle family, including some fruiting species.

clue.text: Remained twisted, tense and obscene

indicators.note: the letters are twisted out of order

parts.note: T = tense, the grammar abbreviation
lewd = obscene

explanation.surface: Someone stayed on, warped, on edge and foul-mouthed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twisted, tense and obscene' reads as three adjectives in a row; the first is the instruction, the other two supply the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwelt is a past tense of dwell, to stay or remain.

clue.text: Rescue one that's been crushed by digger

indicators.note: the one is squeezed inside the digger

parts.note: one who delves, a digger
I = one, set inside DEL…VER

explanation.surface: A rescue is mounted for someone crushed by an excavator.
explanation.walkthrough: A delver is one who delves, an old word for a digger; 'one' is I, as the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver someone is to rescue them, as in 'deliver us from evil'.

clue.text: Brief stint to improve football club before unlimited team growth

indicators.note: cut short by its last letter
without its limits, the first and last letters

parts.note: a bout is a stint; BOUT cut short
to gain is to improve, as in gain strength
Aston Villa, the Birmingham football club

indicators.note: this part comes ahead of the next

parts.note: tEAm without its outer letters

explanation.surface: A short spell of coaching to lift a football club ahead of unrestricted squad expansion.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word reads as football management; 'growth' at the end looks like the club's ambition and is in fact a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Bougainvillaea is a climbing tropical shrub, and a plant is a growth.

clue.text: Partly explain remark legally directed against property

indicators.note: the answer is part of the words that follow

parts.note: explaIN REMark

explanation.surface: A lawyer offers a partial explanation of a comment about property.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans the gap between two words; 'legally' signals that it is a Latin legal phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: In rem is the legal Latin for an action against a thing, such as property, rather than a person.

clue.text: Pointer litter abandoned by female

indicators.note: the female letter leaves the word

parts.note: a farrow is a litter of pigs
F = female, the letter that leaves the litter word

explanation.surface: A pointer dog's litter of puppies has been abandoned by their mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointer' and 'litter' together suggest a gun dog and her pups; the pointer is an arrow and the litter belongs to a pig.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrow is a sign that points the way.

clue.text: Caught male with female cook

indicators.note: the parts go together side by side

parts.note: C = caught, from cricket scoring
he = a male
F = female

explanation.surface: A man is caught in the act with a woman cook.
explanation.walkthrough: C for caught is from cricket scorecards; 'female cook' reads as one unit but splits after 'female'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: chef is the French word for a head cook, now used for any professional cook.

clue.text: Safe place to receive focus of attention

parts.note: to have is to receive, as in 'have a letter'

indicators.note: the focus is the centre point, the middle letter

parts.note: the middle letter of attENtion's nine

explanation.surface: A secure spot where one can get the attention one needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Focus of attention' reads as the centre of interest; here it is literally the centre letter of 'attention'.
explanation.definitionFit: A haven was originally a harbour, where ships shelter from storms, hence any safe place.

clue.text: Grass company really cutting back parts obtained from waste

indicators.note: the letters cut into the grass word

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass

indicators.note: the rear letter is cut off

parts.note: CO = company
VERY without its last letter; CO and VER go inside RE…ED

explanation.surface: A company informer drastically trims spending on waste-derived parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like the verb to inform on someone; it is the plant. 'Cutting back' is two jobs, a container and a shortening.
explanation.definitionFit: Recovered materials are salvaged from waste for reuse.

clue.text: Weapons companies checking defaced equipment

indicators.note: holding back, keeping the other letters within
its face, the first letter, removed

parts.note: firms = companies
GEAR without its first letter, inside FIR…MS

explanation.surface: Arms companies inspect vandalised kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defaced' means the face, or first letter, of GEAR is removed; 'checking' means holding in, as in checking an advance.
explanation.definitionFit: Guns, rifles and pistols are all firearms, one class of weapons.

clue.text: Artist's back pay for services rendered

indicators.note: 'back' as in going back: the payment word is read from its back end to its front

parts.note: a reward is payment for service, and the answer to 1 across

explanation.surface: A painter's back pay for work done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artist's back pay' reads as money owed to a painter; the 's is 'is', and 'back' turns the payment round.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossword-favoured sense: one who draws pictures, alongside the everyday drawer of a desk.
